title: Regulate disability providers in proportion to risk
action: Replace the current registration system with a graduated model in which the level of regulation of each provider matches the risk of the supports it delivers, and align registration and audits with aged care and veterans' care so providers working across sectors are checked once.
why: Heavy registration for low-risk services keeps small providers out, while duplicated audits across care sectors add cost without improving safety.

evidence.source: Working together to deliver the NDIS: Independent Review into the NDIS, Final Report
evidence.quote: The Department of Social Services and the new National Disability Supports Quality and Safeguards Commission should design and implement a graduated risk-proportionate regulatory model for the whole provider market.

evidence.source: Delivering quality care more efficiently: Inquiry report
evidence.quote: establish cross-sectoral registration and audits across the aged care, NDIS and veterans' care sectors, with mutual recognition of registration and audits as an interim step
